decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-12-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka has faced a severe cyclone named 'Ditwa', during the last few days resulting in the loss of hundreds of lives. Further, private and public properties in large extent and infrastructure including highways, bridges, railway tracks, reservoirs, dams, irrigation systems have been severely damaged. As a result, general livelihood has been completely disrupted, and a number of rural industries including paddy cultivation and vegetable cultivation, as well as the fishing industry have been affected. A state of public emergency has been declared across the country as of now, and the affected people are staying in temporary shelters. Beyond the loss of life and property, the heavy rains and floods caused by the cyclone have disrupted services such as water supply, electricity and communication in many areas. Although, the Government is taking measures to expeditiously provide essential services to the affected people with the help of the tri-forces, police, disaster management centers and national and regional administrations, it has been found that these services are not adequate due to the severity of the damage. Although the Government has already allocated Rs.3 billion for emergency disaster relief, it seems that this amount is not sufficient to restore the damage caused to housing, infrastructure, agricultural lands, fisheries and essential services across the country. Therefore, Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Hon. President to establish a fund called the 'Rebuilding Sri Lanka Fund' as a statutory fund operating under the Presidential Secretariat, to receive contributions from donors through a dedicated bank account designated for the said purpose, and to implement a comprehensive mechanism to take necessary steps to restore the lives and livelihoods of the affected people by taking the contributions already received in the accounts of the Treasury and the Central Bank of Sri Lanka as the initial capital of the proposed fund.
